traits.fan_split_depth.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 283): the blade divided to about a third to a half of its radius into single-fold segments.

traits.segment_filaments.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 283): interfold filaments often present; read as a few threads. Its segments are stiff in one plane or variously pendulous, so their posture is left to the species.

traits.petiole_armature.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 283): unarmed tree palms.

traits.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under the genus (Palmae III 4b): fan palms with bisexual flowers.

traits.leaf_division.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments: simple, parted, palmate.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments: simple, parted, palmate.

traits.division_pattern.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. traits.clonal.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: its stems are solitary; its fan leaves are strongly costapalmate, the petiole running on into the blade as a rib.

generator.params.costa.why: The rib the fan's segments rise from, as a share of the frond: a fifth for a strongly costapalmate fan, a tenth for a shortly costapalmate one (the built-in cabbage and California fan palms, 0.18 and 0.12).
